newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs firm as rate fears ease.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs firm as rate fears ease.

text.p: SIMEX Japanese government bond (JGB) and Euroyen futures firmed on Friday as the shadow of a looming interest rate rise appeared to fade.
Dealers said the recent strength of the Japanese yen against the U.S. dollar had helped improve sentiment for JGBs and this had in turn dragged up Euroyen.

"Most of the market now thinks the rumours of a rate hike were not so serious," said a Singaporean dealer with a large U.S. bank. "Certainly we now believe Japanese interest rates will stay roughly similar until the end of the year."
Other dealers quoted analysts as saying there would be no rate hike soon because there were still problems with the Japanese financial sector.
June JGBs settled up 0.51 at 124.20 against their previous 123.70. December Euroyen stood at 98.99 at 1157 GMT against its IMM close at 98.93.
The dollar was quoted at around 115.55 yen early evening in Singapore, against an earlier intraday high of about 117.
"As the dollar/yen comes down, it obviously makes a hike less likely. At least that's the view today," said another dealer.
Most market participants said they were generally waiting until next Tuesday when the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is due to decide whether or not to raise U.S. rates.
"We now think its 40-60 against a rates rise, which is a reversal of the sentiment just a week ago," said a U.S. dealer.
"From now until next Tuesday's FOMC I see range trading and covering of positions but no new big moves," said another.
Eurodollar futures rose slightly through the day, with the December contract ending at 93.735 against its IMM close at 93.715 on 6,142 lots.
